preamble: In Japanese the palatalized voiced sibilant (phonemic /zj/ in yōon syllables, and /z/ before /i/) is realized as the alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] or fricative [ʑ]. The affricate is typical word-initially and after the moraic nasal, the fricative between vowels. Most dialects have also merged original /zi, zj/ with /di, dj/ in this phone (the yotsugana merger), while Tosa keeps /zi/ and /di/ apart.

examples.note: /z/ before /i/ is palatalized and realized as [dʑ ~ ʑ].

sources: Vance, T. J. (2008). The Sounds of Japanese. Cambridge University Press.
context: Japanese /zj/ and /z/ before /i/; [dʑ] word-initially and after the moraic nasal, [ʑ] intervocalically
